findings.title: Unhealthy spawn processes are never killed before a replacement starts
findings.body:
Processes are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which builds a `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and `kill()` is never called.

The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now, when a flusher is detected as hung, the old process keeps running while a new one is spawned for the same shards. Two flushers then work the same Redis shards concurrently, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments. Leaked processes also pile up on every restart.

Fix: check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` (or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`).

findings.title: join() never terminates spawn processes
findings.body: The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check in `join()` has the same flaw: `SpawnProcess` is not a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`. As a result, `terminate()` is never called on flusher processes that are still alive after the wait loop. Lingering flushers can keep flushing shards that have been reassigned to another consumer after a rebalance or shutdown.

findings.title: join() skips cleanup of remaining processes once the deadline passes
findings.body:
`next_step.join(timeout)` can use up the whole timeout. After that, the per-process loop hits `break` on `remaining_time <= 0` and leaves the loop without terminating any remaining processes. With N flusher processes, any not yet visited stay alive and are never terminated.

The deadline should only cap the wait. Termination of every process should still happen after the loop.

findings.title: Memory info is queried once per flusher buffer
findings.body:
`get_memory_info()` is called on every per-process `SpansBuffer`. If these buffers share the same Redis cluster, every node's memory is queried and summed N times on each `submit`.

The ratio stays correct, but this adds N-fold Redis INFO calls on the consumer's main thread, which this PR is trying to keep minimal. Querying once (e.g. via the original buffer) would be sufficient.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key (`shards` vs `shard`)
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the tag key `shards`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `shard`. This makes it awkward to correlate these metrics in dashboards. Use one key consistently.

findings.title: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` is never used
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` is not called anywhere. Restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards` directly, so this method should be removed.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test sets `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at the start, so the added `time.sleep(0.1)`, meant to "give flusher threads time to process", does nothing. The test still depends on `join()` busy-waiting. The comment is misleading, and the test may be flaky if it relies on this delay.

findings.title: Unrelated documentation change bundled in PR
findings.body: The hasattr/isinstance anti-pattern added to CLAUDE.md has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher. It should go in a separate PR.
